title: Is every link the same vote?
hook: X has 3 in-links, Y has 2. Does the count decide which page ranks higher?

knows: counting in-links is one way to rank pages
doesNotKnow: that a link counts for more when it comes from a page that lists other good pages

misconception: The page with the most in-links ranks highest.
objective: The learner can explain that in hubs and authorities a page's authority is the sum of the hub scores of the lists pointing at it, and a list's hub score is the sum of the authority scores it points to, so on this graph Y (2 in-links from strong lists) ends at 0.277 while X (3 in-links, mostly from lists that name only X) ends at 0.099.

claims.text: After 50 updates Y's authority score is 0.277 and X's is 0.099, though X has 3 in-links and Y has 2; W, also with 3 in-links, ends highest at 0.346.
claims.source: Demo.tsx hits(): links h1, h2 -> Y, Z, W; h3, h4 -> X; h5 -> X, W. Round 0: hubs 0.2 each, authority = in-link counts normalised (X 0.300, W 0.300, Y 0.200, Z 0.200). Each update: hub = sum of the authority scores it points to, then authority = sum of hub scores pointing at it, each normalised to sum 1. Builder's node re-run of the same loop (scratchpad ncmc/hits.mjs), 2026-10-14: after 50 updates Y 0.277, Z 0.277, W 0.346, X 0.099; hubs h1 0.368, h2 0.368, h5 0.182, h3 0.041, h4 0.041. Settled to 3 decimals by update 10. Matches brief cs.algorithms NCM #2 (which updates authority first; the 50-round values agree). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): VERIFIED. Own node (fc21/hits.mjs), same update order (hub then authority, normalised to sum 1): after 50 updates X 0.099, Y 0.277, Z 0.277, W 0.346; already settled at update 10. W highest, X lowest, as the reveal says.

claims.text: Starting from in-link counts, X (0.300) scores above Y (0.200).
claims.source: In-link counts X 3, W 3, Y 2, Z 2, total 10, normalised to sum 1 (Demo.tsx IN, round 0). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): VERIFIED. In-link counts X 3, W 3, Y 2, Z 2 of 10: X 0.300, Y 0.200 at round 0 (own run).

claims.text: A page's authority score is the sum of the hub scores of the pages pointing to it, and a page's hub score is the sum of the authority scores of the pages it points to (then each is normalised); each score feeds the other.
claims.source: Easley & Kleinberg (2010), Networks, Crowds, and Markets, ch. 14 (hubs and authorities); Kleinberg J. (1999), 'Authoritative sources in a hyperlinked environment', J. ACM 46(5). recall.question: Two pages each get 3 links. Page P's links come from lists that link only to P; page Q's come from lists that also link to many well-linked pages. Under hubs and authorities, which ends with more authority?
options: Q, because its links come from strong lists
P, because its fans are loyal to it alone
A tie: same number of links
recall.why: Authority adds up the hub scores of the lists pointing at a page, and a list is a strong hub when it points to strong pages. Lists that name only one page stay weak hubs, so their links carry little weight.
